findings.reason: Untrusted source: hostif = interface->cur_altsetting captured at gigaset_probe entry (line 657); its endpoint[] flex-array length is solely the descriptor-declared bNumEndpoints of the altsetting a physically attacker-controlled USB gadget presents at enumeration, and drivers/usb/core/config.c allocates only bNumEndpoints entries (leaving the pointer NULL for a 0-endpoint altsetting). Missing guarantee: gigaset_probe validates only bInterfaceNumber==0, bAlternateSetting==0 and bInterfaceClass==255 (lines 670-686), then takes fixed assumed indices &hostif->endpoint[0].desc at line 708 and &hostif->endpoint[1].desc at line 727 with no bNumEndpoints >= 2 check anywhere in usb-gigaset.c (grep of the whole file returns zero bNumEndpoints occurrences). Unsafe use: the OOB-reachable endpoint[0].desc.wMaxPacketSize becomes buffer_size that sizes ucs->bulk_out_buffer = kmalloc(buffer_size) (lines 709-713) and usb_endpoint_num(endpoint) sets bulk_out_epnum (line 712) used for the bulk-out pipe; endpoint[1].desc.wMaxPacketSize (line 737) sizes ucs->rcvbuf = kmalloc(buffer_size) (line 739), and usb_fill_int_urb (lines 742-746) programs usb_rcvintpipe(udev, usb_endpoint_num(endpoint)) plus endpoint->bInterval from the unvalidated descriptor, with the URB submitted at line 748 (usb_submit_urb) at device plug-in. A gadget spoofing the Siemens M105 vendor/product ID (the only ID check at line 669-673) with a 0/1-endpoint altsetting yields NULL-deref or OOB read past the endpoint array at probe; the OOB-read wMaxPacketSize/bInterval/bEndpointAddress directly program kmalloc sizes, a pipe, and a live interrupt URB. Counterevidence checked: zero bNumEndpoints references in the whole file; the only gates are interface number/altsetting/class checks that do not constrain endpoint count. Sibling bas-gigaset.c likewise has zero bNumEndpoints occurrences.

Untrusted source: iface_desc = &interface->altsetting[0] captured at sur40_probe; its endpoint[] flex-array is sized solely by the descriptor-declared bNumEndpoints of altsetting 0, which a physically attacker-controlled USB gadget controls at enumeration. Missing guarantee: sur40_probe indexes endpoint[4] with a fixed literal 4 (line 531) after checking only bInterfaceClass == 0xFF; grep of the whole file returns zero bNumEndpoints occurrences, so nothing validates that the altsetting declares at least 5 endpoints. Unsafe use: the descriptor is dereferenced immediately - endpoint->bEndpointAddress is compared against TOUCH_ENDPOINT (line 532) and then sur40->bulk_in_size = usb_endpoint_maxp(endpoint) and sur40->bulk_in_epaddr = endpoint->bEndpointAddress (lines 570-571) program the polled-input read path whose URB uses usb_rcvbulkpipe(sur40->usbdev, sur40->bulk_in_epaddr), and the maxp value sizes sur40->bulk_in_buffer = kmalloc(sur40->bulk_in_size) (lines 572-573). A gadget spoofing the Samsung SUR40 vendor/product ID with a class-0xFF interface declaring fewer than 5 endpoints makes endpoint[4] an out-of-bounds read past the flex array (or NULL-deref for a 0-endpoint altsetting) at device plug-in, feeding an OOB-read maxp into a kmalloc size and an OOB-read bEndpointAddress into a bulk-in pipe. Counterevidence checked: no bNumEndpoints guard anywhere in the file; the only class check does not constrain endpoint count.

findings.reason: Untrusted source: actconfig->interface[0]->altsetting[0].desc.bNumEndpoints and the variable-length endpoint[] flex array of interface 0 altsetting 0 are descriptor data supplied at enumeration by a physically attacker-controlled USB device (usbcore allocates only bNumEndpoints entries and leaves the array NULL when num_ep == 0). Missing guarantee: grep over the whole file shows bNumEndpoints occurs 0 times in ueagle-atm.c, and uea_bind only checks ifnum == UEA_INTR_IFACE_NO (0), never the endpoint count; no code path validates that altsetting[0] declares at least 1 endpoint before endpoint[0] is read inline in the usb_fill_int_urb argument list (lines 2206-2210). Unsafe use: the unvalidated index-0 descriptor's bInterval is installed as the polling interval of sc->urb_int, which is immediately usb_submit_urb'd (line 2212) at device plug-in (usbatm_usb_probe -> uea_bind -> uea_boot). A malicious gadget matching the Eagle/ADI ADSL modem device table with bNumEndpoints == 0 on interface 0 makes endpoint[0] a read past a never-allocated (NULL) endpoint array - a NULL-derived wild pointer dereference at plug-in - or past a short array, and the garbage bInterval is installed as the live interrupt URB's polling interval. Interface/altsetting levels are structurally in-bounds (interface[0] exists for any accepted config); the violation is the unvalidated endpoint index. Counterevidence checked: zero bNumEndpoints occurrences in the file; UEA_INTR_PIPE is a hardcoded endpoint address, only the bInterval is taken from the unvalidated endpoint[0].

Untrusted source: iface_desc = interface->cur_altsetting captured at usb_pcwd_probe; the endpoint[] array length is the device-declared bNumEndpoints at enumeration (config.c leaves it NULL for a 0-endpoint altsetting). Missing guarantee: usb_pcwd_probe checks only bInterfaceClass == USB_CLASS_HID before taking &iface_desc->endpoint[0].desc at line 634; grep of pcwd_usb.c returns zero bNumEndpoints occurrences, so nothing validates that the HID-class interface declares at least 1 endpoint - a legal USB HID interface altsetting may declare bNumEndpoints == 0, making endpoint[0] a read past a NULL array. Unsafe use: endpoint->bEndpointAddress programs pipe = usb_rcvintpipe(udev, endpoint->bEndpointAddress) and endpoint->wMaxPacketSize sets usb_pcwd->intr_size, which sizes usb_pcwd->intr_buffer = usb_alloc_coherent(udev, usb_pcwd->intr_size) and feeds the interrupt URB submitted at probe; the usb_endpoint_is_int_in(endpoint) check reads the same unvalidated descriptor. Medium confidence because the int-in type check gates pipe use but not the OOB read/NULL-deref itself. Counterevidence checked: zero bNumEndpoints in file; only class gate exists.

Untrusted source: hwarc_neep_init reads iface->cur_altsetting->endpoint[0].desc where iface is the probed UWB radio-control interface; the endpoint array length is the device-declared bNumEndpoints and usbcore leaves it NULL when the altsetting declares 0 endpoints. Missing guarantee: grep of hwa-rc.c returns zero bNumEndpoints occurrences, and hwarc_probe performs no endpoint-count validation before hwarc_neep_init runs during probe. Unsafe use: epd->bEndpointAddress and epd->bInterval are used directly in usb_fill_int_urb(usb_rcvintpipe(usb_dev, epd->bEndpointAddress), ..., epd->bInterval) and the URB is submitted immediately - a 0-endpoint altsetting makes &endpoint[0] a NULL-derived wild pointer dereference at probe, and a short array gives an OOB-read bInterval installed as the notification URB's polling interval. Medium confidence: reachability requires a UWB HWA radio-controller gadget (usb_host class) and the probe chain was verified at the function level but the exact caller ordering was not deep-read line-by-line in this bounded pass. Counterevidence checked: zero bNumEndpoints occurrences in the file.

limitations: No compilation, Kconfig check, or USB-gadget reproducer was run: the snapshot is read-only and builds would go under $TMPDIR only; all findings are static source hypotheses supported by exact line reads and grep-proven absence of bNumEndpoints guards (zero occurrences in each reported file).

drivers/isdn/gigaset/bas-gigaset.c endpoint[0] read (zero bNumEndpoints occurrences in the file, after usb_set_interface to altsetting 3) is structurally the same mechanism as finding 1 but was not separately deep-read within the finalize call budget; it should be treated as a co-located variant in follow-up triage.

The full sweep of sound/usb, drivers/hid, drivers/input, drivers/staging, drivers/iio, drivers/uwb (beyond hwa-rc), drivers/platform, drivers/nfc, drivers/bluetooth and remaining trees for endpoint[] fixed-index reads was cut short by the finalize instruction: the drivers/usb subtree (class, misc, serial, storage, atm, wusbcore) and gigaset/sur40/pcwd/hwa-rc were covered by grep + targeted reads, but sound/usb fixed altsetting[1]/endpoint sites and staging USB drivers (other than those reachable in the sweep) were not exhaustively line-verified.

cdc-acm.c fixed indices at 1326-1328 (epctrl/epread/epwrite) sit after a bNumEndpoints-bounded data-interface scan but the control-interface endpoint[0] fetch was not verified line-by-line against an explicit bNumEndpoints == 1 guard in this snapshot; recorded as reviewed-not-fully-verified (safe-leaning) rather than reported.

The exact fault mode for a 0-endpoint altsetting depends on usbcore allocation details (drivers/usb/core/config.c allocates alt->endpoint only when num_ep > 0): NULL-deref vs adjacent-heap OOB read; the direction of the invariant violation is certain, the exact fault is not.

hwa-rc.c reachability requires a UWB HWA radio-controller gadget (USB_CLASS_PHYSICAL/host class) whose probe chain calls hwarc_neep_init; the caller ordering was verified at the function level but not with a full line-level call trace in this pass.

Interface/altsetting-count gaps (actconfig->interface[idx] without bNumInterfaces, num_altsetting assumptions) were excluded per the branch split and belong to the if-alt-count branch; ueagle-atm.c:2210's interface[0]/altsetting[0] levels are structurally in-bounds and only its endpoint[0] read is reported here.
